messages:
anna: heads up — we had two tenants hit >800ms p99 during the EU dc drain this morning. root cause: fallback chain sent writes to a geo that was allowed for compute but not for PII, so requests retried + queued. :grimacing:
jordan: ugh. can you paste the trace or quick logs?
anna: gist of logs: many 409/consent-fail then client retry -> longer tail. no huge error spike, just latency. snippet: `POST /v1/infer -> 200  but backend latency 620ms -> fallback to eu-west-2 increased to 980ms`
mike: is this the residency flag mismatch we've seen? tenant metadata consent vs runtime routing policy mismatch?
anna: exactly. a tenant had consent:pending in control plane but dataplane fallback assumed compute-compatible. so fallback routing didn't honor consent gating.
sasha: legally we can’t move PII out of the primary region unless tenant.consent == "allowed". pending means keep-local or deny. not allowed to just fall back.
jordan: so current behavior is: if primary overloaded, route to next region based on latency/capacity (no consent check), which is wrong. we need precedence: consent check before region selection.
mike: agree. implementation options: (A) fail fast with 4xx when consent disallows fallback; (B) route to a compatible queued path in same region (degrade), (C) allow operator-ordered evacuations with explicit consent overrides for emergencies. tradeoffs: A is simplest and predictable but user-visible errors. B preserves availability but increases unit cost. C is emergency-only and needs auditable flow.
anna: for immediate fix we should change routing to consult tenant.consentset during selection and prevent cross-region writes unless explicit. low risk.
jordan: plus we need operator guidance for planned drains to avoid user-facing 4xx. current operator flow just cordons and scale down; we should add a staged evacuation ordering.
anna: proposed runbook (short):
1) mark region as "cordon:prewarm" -> prevent new tenant-primary allocations but keep topologies warm
2) prewarm fallback-compatible KV caches in target regions for tenants with consent==allowed
3) for tenants with consent==pending, create per-tenant hold: set tenant.eviction_priority = "defer" and add operator note
4) scheduled slow-drain: 30m window per shard, monitor p50/p95/p99 and consent-fail counts
5) only after explicit manual approval mark tenant as movable (consent=allowed) or keep pinned

mike: can we express the per-tenant metadata as part of the residency API? something like: 
```json
{"tenant_id":"t-1234","residency": {"consent":"pending","eviction_priority":"normal","allowed_regions":["eu-west-2"]}}
```
that way routing can check allowed_regions + consent flag quickly (no CP roundtrip).
sasha: legal ok with that shape as long as there’s an audit trail and the default for missing consent is "deny cross-region write". also need retention of consent change history.
jordan: ops telemetry asks: emit two new metrics: residency_fallback_blocked_total{tenant_id,region} and residency_fallback_latency_ms{tenant_id,from_region,to_region}. need alert when blocked_total > 10/min for any tenant.
anna: will add those counters. also suggest a fallback-mode toggle: `allow_fallback_default = false` on proxy to avoid surprises while we roll this.
mike: implementation plan: 1) quick prod-safe check in proxy: consult cached tenant residency metadata (fast path), if denied -> return 409 with structured error code residency.blocked; 2) add metrics; 3) update operator runbook to use eviction_priority tags; 4) follow-up RFC for long-term: affinity scoring + operator-assignable evacuation buckets.
jordan: can we do a small canary? deploy-bot: Canary scheduled to eu-canary at 2024-05-14T09:30Z for routing proxy flag `allow_fallback_default=false` (rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100%) :rocket:
anna: canary SGTM. i'll add a tiny migration script to populate eviction_priority for known tenants and set defaults.
sasha: legal: put me on the RFC review. i want examples of the audit events and the UI flow for customers to change consent.
mike: i'll own the proxy change, anna will own runbook and migration, jordan will own metrics/alerts, sasha legal reviewer, i'll draft RFC after canary.
anna: one more operator detail — evacuation ordering: prioritize shards by memory pressure -> active sessions -> consent_deferred. so we only evict low-memory, low-session tenants first. helps avoid user impact.
jordan: note: also need to surface a per-shard "evacuation_score" in telemetry so operator can reorder quickly.
mike: adding that to telemetry list.
anna: ok i'll open a short RFC with code pointers and the runbook fragment, link to canary, and assign owners.
deploy-bot: RFC created at https://go.redwood/rfcs/1234 (draft) by mike.
anna: :thumbsup: thanks team. plan to monitor canary and sync tomorrow 10:00am PT.
